This petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act 1988 by the petitioner praying to award compensation of Rs. 15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, I,e.,
lorry bearing registration No. AP-02-TD-2895, near Jathavarahosalli Village Gate,
Chickballapur on 07.07.2022 at about 1.50 to 1.55 a.m.

entities.text: Syed Khaleel Alias Syed Khaleel Basha
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: Due to the accident the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
2. Prior to an accident he was hale and healthy and he was working as cleaner and earning a sum of Rs. 15,000/- p.m.
After the accident he was not able to perform his work.
Therefore he sustained loss of income from the date of accident.
Therefore the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
3. In response to the notice, respondent no.1 and 2 have appeared through the counsel and filed written statement.
4. Respondent no.1 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further it admitted the issuance of the policy and denied the occurrence of the accident.

Further it contended that the driver of lorry had no valid driving license to drive the vehicle at the time of accident and also not having valid RC,FC permit insurance etc., to ply the same in the place of accident.
Further it contended that the amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive and without any base.
Hence prayed for dismissal of the petition with exemplary cost.
5. Respondent no.2 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Respondent no.2 denied the occurrence of the accident and contended that the amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive and without any base.
Hence prayed for dismissal of the petition with exemplary cost.
6. On the basis of rival pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed.

1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident that occurred on 07.07.2022 due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of goods carrier lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-02-TD- 2895?

7. In order to prove his case he got examined as P.W.1 and got marked 15 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
Dr. Chidanand K.J got examined as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P16 and Ex.P17.

The Medical Record Technician by name Shaik Mohammed Umar got examined as PW.3 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.P18 to Ex.P20.
8.
Heard arguments and perused the records.

9. After assessing the oral as well as documentary evidence my findings on the above Issues are as fallows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

:: REASONS ::
Issue No.1:-
10.
To prove the rash and negligent act of driving on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-02- TD-2895, the petitioner relied upon the his oral evidence and police records.

11. The Ex.P1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the complaint, E.P3 is the spot Mahazar, Ex.P4 is the spot sketch,
Ex.P7 is the IMV report, Ex.P.9 is the charge sheet.
12. By going through the above said police record it clearly discloses the occurrence of the accident and the identity of the lorry.
The charge sheet also speaks that the driver of the lorry drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control and dashed to the railway bridge and turtled on the road.
Due to the accident the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore this court is of the opinion that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the lorry.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
Issue No.2:-
13. In this case petitioner has claimed total compensation of Rs. 15,00,000/- lakhs for the injuries sustained by him in an accident on various heads.

14. In the decision reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 (Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another) Division Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court has laid down on what grounds compensation is required to be awarded in personal injury case.

entities.text: (2011) 1 SCC 343 (Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another) Division Bench
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In para 6 of the said judgment their Lordships have demarcated the heads under which compensation is required to be considered which reads as here under:
Syed Khaleel Alias Syed Khaleel Basha vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96449977/
3 6.

entities.text: Syed Khaleel Alias Syed Khaleel Basha vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages(Special damages) (i)Expenses relating to treatment,
hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

(iii) future medical expenses Nonpecuniary damages(General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life(shortening of normal longevity)
15.

From going through the above said decision, it is clear that under the pecuniary damages expenses relating to the treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure are required to be considered with.
In the second head loss of earning and other gains of the injured person is required to be considered.
In the background of principles laid down by their Lordships in the above said decision we can have to consider the quantum of compensation for which the petitioner is entitled to.
16. LOSS OF INCOME -
It is the case of the petitioner that he has sustained permanent disability due to injury sustained in an accident.
In order to prove the same the petitioner relied on the evidence of PW2 and documents produced by him.

PW.2 deposed that the petitioner has sustained Grade 2 compound bi condylar proximal tibia fracture, grade 111 a compound lisfranc fracture foot and underwent surgery of ORIF with K wire for foot.
17.

PW.2 further deposed that there is a restriction in the range of movements of left knee and ankle,
quadriceps wasting is seen, associated with pain on movements knee and ankle.
The X-rays shows the fracture united with implant insitu.
The PW.3 also observed that the petitioner is finding difficulty in sitting, squatting and other co-ordinated activities.
The petitioner was working as cleaner.
This job requires to do lot of physical activities.
So the above mentioned difficulties certainly will effect the work of petitioner.
Therefore I assess the functional disability of petitioner at 16%.
18. It is the specific case of the petitioner that prior to the accident he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, by considering the nature of work the income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m.

4 19.

sentences.text: Furthermore, Hon'ble Supreme Court in a full bench decision reported in 2020 SCC ONLINE 752, (PAPPU DEO YADAV V.S NARESH KUMAR AND OTHERS)

entities.text: PAPPU DEO YADAV V.S NARESH KUMAR AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: held that, even in case of permanent partial disability, amount towards future prospects can be awarded.
The said preposition of law has been reiterated by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a decision reported in 2020 SCC ONLINE KAR 1446, (ALAMELI BAI V.S MANAGING DIRECTOR, K.S.R.T.C.).

entities.text: 2020 SCC ONLINE KAR 1446, (ALAMELI BAI V.S MANAGING DIRECTOR, K.S.R.T.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein at Paragraph No. 10 it is held that, even in case of functional disability cases future prospects can be awarded.
Thus, petitioner is entitled for the amount towards future prospects.
Thus, notional income comes to Rs. 15,000/- + 40% (Rs. 6,000/-) = 21,000/-.

Thus, income comes to Rs. 21,000/-
per month.
20. The Ex
. P12 Notarized copy of Aadhar card the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 1988 and the accident occurred in the year of 2022.
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of an accident petitioner was aged 34 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 16.
So future loss of income=( monthly income + future prospects) x 12 months x multiplier x disability, i.e., 21,000x12x16x15%= Rs.6,04,800/-.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled to Rs.6,04,800/- towards loss of future income due to permanent disability.
21. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS AND LOSS OF AMENITIES -
To prove what are the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, he has relied on the wound certificate, discharge summary, the medical bills, medical prescriptions and X-rays.

By going through wound certificate and discharge summary, it is clear that petitioner has sustained Grade II compoun bi condylar proximal tibia fracture right side and Grade 111 A compound lisfrence injury to right foot and underwent surgeries.

22. In the decision reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 (Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another), the Hon'ble Apex Court made an observation about the general principles relating to compensation in a injury cases.

entities.text: (2011) 1 SCC 343 (Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases.

The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible,
fully and adeuately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned"

5 23.

sentences.text: Therefore the duty lies upon this court to award just compensation.
Due to injuries the petitioner has lost the amenities and enjoyment of life.
Thus, he might have been forced to incur amount towards amenities and nutritional food.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, it would be just and reasonable to award an amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- to the petitioner towards Pain and sufferings and loss of amenities of life.
24. FOOD AND NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES -
From the discharge summaries at Ex.P.9, it is clear that petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 09.07.2022 to 12.07.2022 for 4 days.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.4,000/- is awarded to the petitioner towards food and nourishment and attendant charges.
25. MEDICAL EXPENSES - It is the case of the petitioner that he has spent huge money for his treatment.
26. In Ex.P13, petitioner has produced medical bill for Rs. 1200/-.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,200/- towards Medical Expenses.

27. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, it might not be possible for him to discharge any work minimum for a period of 2 months.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of income during Laid up period.
28. TRANSPORTATION CHARGES -
The petitioner has taken follow up treatment even after his discharge from the hospital and he has visited the doctor.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded to petitioner towards Transportation charges.
29.FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES -
During the course of cross-examination of PW.2, he has deposed that petitioner is has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses.

30. In all I am going to award compensation of Rs. 7,85,000/- under the following heads:
1. Loss of future income due Rs. 6,04,800/-
to permanent disabilities 2. Pain and sufferings & Loss Rs. 1,00,000/-
of amenities.
3. Food and nourishment Rs. 4,000/-

6 and attendant charges

4. Medical Expenses Rs. 1,200/-
5. Loss of income during Laid Rs. 30,000/-
up period

6. Transportation Charges Rs. 15,000/-
7.

Future Medical bills Rs. 30,000/-
Total Rs. 7,85,000/-
31.
LIABILITY- There is no dispute with regard to insurance coverage of the offending vehicle as could be seen from pleadings.
Therefore respondent no.2 being owner of the offending vehicle insured with respondent no.1 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
However the primary liability is upon the respondent no.1 to pay the compensation.
In view of the same respondent no.1 has to deposit the compensation amount before the tribunal.
Hence I have answered Point No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:-

32 . In view of the discussions made supra, I proceed to pass the following:
:: ORDER ::
The claim petition under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act filed by the petitioner against respondents is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is awarded total compensation of Rs.7,85,000/- (Rupees - Seven Lakhs Eighty Five Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the deposit of the amount in the Tribunal.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent no.1- Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within one month from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount 25% of the share of petitioner, shall be invested in fixed deposit in his name for a period of three years in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice with a liberty to withdraw accrued interest periodically.
